readings.title: YeHoVaH Answers from the Whirlwind
readings.subtitle: Where were you when I laid the earth's foundations?
readings.text: [Job 38:1] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered Iyoḇ out of the whirlwind, and said, [2] <dq>Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge? [3] Now gird up <dn>your</dn> loins like a man, and <dn>I</dn> ask <dn>you</dn>, and <dn>you</dn> answer <dn>Me</dn>. [4] Where were <dn>you</dn> when <dn>I</dn> laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if <dn>you</dn> have understanding. [5] Who set its measurements, if <dn>you</dn> know? Or who stretched the line upon it? [6] Upon what were its foundations sunk? Or who laid its corner-stone, [7] when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> shouted for joy? [8] Or who enclosed the sea with doors, when it burst forth and came from the womb; [9] when <dn>I</dn> made the clouds its garment, and thick darkness its swaddling band; [10] and assigned for it <dn>My</dn> law, and set bars and doors; [11] and said, ‘This far <dn>you</dn> have come, but no farther, and here <dn>your</dn> proud waves stop?’</dq>

readings.title: Commanding the Dawn
readings.subtitle: Have you entered the gates of death or the dwelling of light?
readings.text: [Job 38:12] <dq>Have <dn>you</dn> ever commanded the morning, and caused the dawn to know its place, [13] to take hold of the ends of the earth, and the wrong be shaken out of it? [14] It is changed like clay under a seal, and they stand out like a garment. [15] And their light is withheld from the wrong, and the arm lifted up is broken. [16] Have <dn>you</dn> come to the sources of the sea? Or have <dn>you</dn> walked about in the recesses of the deep? [17] Were the gates of death revealed to <dn>you</dn>? Or have <dn>you</dn> seen the gates of the shadow of death? [18] Have <dn>you</dn> understood the breadth of the earth? Declare, if <dn>you</dn> know it all. [19] Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place, [20] that <dn>you</dn> should take it to its boundary, and know the paths to its home? [21] Do <dn>you</dn> know? For <dn>you</dn> would have been born then, and the number of <dn>your</dn> days been many!</dq>

readings.title: The Storehouses of Heaven
readings.subtitle: Do you know the laws of the heavens?
readings.text: [Job 38:22] <dq>Have <dn>you</dn> entered into the storehouses of snow, or have <dn>you</dn> seen the storehouses of hail, [23] which <dn>I</dn> have kept for the time of distress, for the day of fighting and battle? [24] Where is the way that light is divided, or the east wind scattered over the earth? [25] Who has cleft a channel for the overflowing water, or a way for the thunderclaps, [26] to make rain fall on land where no one is, a wilderness in which there is no man; [27] to satisfy the wild and waste places, and to make the seeds of grass to sprout? [28] Does the rain have a father? Or who has brought forth the drops of dew? [29] From whose belly comes the ice? And who gave birth to the frost of the heavens? [30] The waters harden like stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen. [31] Do <dn>you</dn> bind the bands of Kimah, or loosen the cords of Kesil? [32] Do <dn>you</dn> bring out the constellations in its season? Or do <dn>you</dn> lead the Bear with its sons? [33] Do <dn>you</dn> know the laws of the heavens? Or do <dn>you</dn> set their rule over the earth? [34] Do <dn>you</dn> lift up <dn>your</dn> voice to the clouds, so that floods of water cover <dn>you</dn>? [35] Do <dn>you</dn> send out lightnings, and they go and say to <dn>you</dn>, ‘Here we are!’? [36] Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the heart? [37] Who has wisdom to count the clouds, or to tip over the bottles of the heavens, [38] when the dust hardens in clumps, and the clods cling together?</dq>

readings.title: Provision for the Wild
readings.subtitle: Who provides food for the raven?
readings.text: [Job 38:39] <dq>Do <dn>you</dn> hunt the prey for the lion, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions, [40] when they crouch in dens, sit in the cover of their hiding place? [41] Who provides food for the raven, when its young ones cry to <dn>Ěl</dn>, and wander about without food?</dq>

readings.title: The Freedom of Wild Animals
readings.subtitle: Who set the wild donkey free?
readings.text: [Job 39:1] <dq>Do <dn>you</dn> know the time when the wild mountain goats bear young? Or do <dn>you</dn> observe when the deer gives birth? [2] Do <dn>you</dn> number the months they complete? Or do <dn>you</dn> know the time when they bear young? [3] They bow down, they bring forth their young, their labour pains are ended. [4] Their young ones are thriving, they grow up in the field. They shall leave and shall not return to them. [5] Who set the wild donkey free? Who loosed the bonds of the wild donkey, [6] whose home <dn>I</dn> have made the desert, and the salt land his dwelling? [7] He laughs at the commotion of the city; he does not hear the shouts of the driver. [8] The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searches for all that is green. [9] Would the wild ox be pleased to serve <dn>you</dn>? Or spend the night by <dn>your</dn> feeding trough? [10] If <dn>you</dn> bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes, would he plough the valleys behind <dn>you</dn>? [11] Would <dn>you</dn> rely on his great strength? Or would <dn>you</dn> leave <dn>your</dn> labour to him? [12] Would <dn>you</dn> trust him to bring home <dn>your</dn> grain, and gather it to <dn>your</dn> threshing-floor?</dq>

readings.title: The Ostrich and the War Horse
readings.subtitle: Have you given the horse strength?
readings.text: [Job 39:13] <dq>The wings of the ostrich flap joyously, but they are not the pinions and plumage of a stork! [14] She leaves her eggs on the ground, and warms them in the dust; [15] and she forgets that a foot might crush them, or a wild beast tread on them. [16] She treats her young harshly, as if not hers; her toil is in vain, without fear, [17] because <dn>Eloah</dn> has made her forget wisdom, and did not endow her with understanding. [18] When she lifts herself on high, she laughs at the horse and its rider. [19] Have <dn>you</dn> given the horse strength? Have <dn>you</dn> covered his neck with a mane? [20] Would <dn>you</dn> make him leap like a locust? His splendid snorting is frightening. [21] He paws in the valley, and rejoices in strength. He gallops into the clash of arms. [22] He laughs at fear, and is not frightened; nor does he turn back from the sword. [23] The quiver rattles against him, the glittering spear and lance. [24] He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, and he does not stand still because of a voice of a shophar. [25] At the blast of the shophar he says, ‘Aha!’ And from afar he smells the battle, the thunder of commanders and shouting.</dq>

readings.title: The Birds of Prey
readings.subtitle: Does the hawk fly by your wisdom?
readings.text: [Job 39:26] <dq>Does the hawk fly by <dn>your</dn> wisdom, spreading its wings toward the south? [27] Does the eagle mount up at <dn>your</dn> mouth, and make its nest on high? [28] It dwells on the rock, and lodges on the crag of the rock and the stronghold. [29] From there it searches out the prey, its eyes see it from afar. [30] And its young ones suck up blood. And where the slain are, there it is!</dq>

readings.title: The Almighty's Rebuke
readings.subtitle: Should a reprover contend with the Almighty?
readings.text: [Job 40:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered Iyoḇ, and said, [2] <dq>Should a reprover contend with the Almighty? Let him who reproves <dn>Eloah</dn> answer it.</dq>

readings.title: Job's Humble Reply
readings.subtitle: I lay my hand over my mouth.
readings.text: [Job 40:3] And Iyoḇ answered <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, [4] “See, I am insignificant, what would I answer <dn>You</dn>? I lay my hand over my mouth. [5] Once I have spoken, but I have no answer – and twice, but I say no more.”
